report:
K29 FINDINGS: universal zeros in P (LOOPY section 8, open question 6)
(K29 completed 2026-10-29 in a second pass. Starting state: VERIFY.md. The harness refused to write FINDINGS.md, so this is findings.txt; the same text is in summary.json.)

SUMMARY (5 lines)
1. YES, inside a stated boundary. Frozen groups with T_P >= 2 on both sides exist that act as 0 beside EVERY context of the class "at most 2 pawns a side, ranks 2-5, on the files at distance >= 2 from F_Z". On cyl:7x6 (F_Z = a-c, contexts on e,f: 885 contexts, both sides to move) four symmetry classes (14 groups) do, e.g. Kb3 Pa2 Pc2 kb1 pa3 pc3 (T_P = 4 for White to move, 5 for Black). CHECKED-2: kp_p --pmodel and ref3 agree on every Phi, kpsolve --frozen and ref3 --frozen agree on every Psi, 0 contexts differ.
2. Counts. 1,236 candidate groups = 446 symmetry classes in 10 configurations. 269 classes fail: each has a witness context, all 269 confirmed by two solver pairs, plus a sample of 96 non-representative class members, all confirmed. 107 classes survive the context set stated per configuration (section 4) and all 107 were re-checked on that whole set by two solver pairs: 0 differences. Survival is not universality: 2 of the 4 cyl:7x6 survivors lose the zero beside Pf2 pf3 pf4 pf5 (1 white and 3 black pawns; CONFIRMED); the other 2 had no failing context among the first 2,682 of the 3,237 contexts with at most 3 pawns a side (all 2,677 contexts with at most 5 pawns in total, and 5 more).
3. Failure mechanism (269 classes, 271 witness lines): the mover that loses in the frozen model escapes in P by a king step onto the buffer file (124), is stalemated because a context pawn covers every buffer square its group can step to (47), steps with the king inside F_Z (45), or moves a pawn (8); in 47 more lines the frozen winner is refuted by the opponent's king move (34 to the buffer, 13 inside F_Z). 267 of the 269 first failing contexts have a pawn on the file next to the buffer.
4. NOT shown: no hand proof; the survivors are not proved universal zeros (CONJECTURE); the context class is a restriction (no e.p. right at the root, ranks 2-5, nothing on the buffer files, at most 2 pawns a side, one or two context files for the wide boards). "No universal zero" is NOT the result; "universal zero" is the result only for the class named.
5. Files: data/table_all.tsv (every class, outcome, witness, mechanism), data/survivors.txt, EDITS.md, summary.json, scripts/, logs/.

1. DEFINITIONS
Setting. Board W x 6, flat or cylinder (kings/SPEC.md). F_Z = files zs .. zs+fz-1 (cyl: mod W). The distance of a file to F_Z is the file distance (cyl: around the seam); the buffer is the files at distance 1. A context H is a set of pawns of both colours on files at distance >= 2 from F_Z (grp --dmin 2; the d3 runs use distance >= 3, a buffer two files wide), on ranks 2-5 (all pawn ranks of a 6-rank board), at most 2 white and at most 2 black pawns (the "c3" run: 3 and 3), distinct squares. No e.p. right at the root. Both sides to move.
Phi and Psi (K23). Phi(Z+H) = the pair (White to move, Black to move) of P results from White's view (kp_p --pmodel: a promotion ends the game; real kings; stalemate is a draw). Psi(H) = the same pair in the frozen model (kpsolve --frozen: a king move loses at once, a promotion wins at once, stalemate draws), computed on H with two parked kings.
"Z acts as 0 beside H (in P)" iff Phi(Z+H) = Psi(H) as pairs. Z is a "universal zero for a context class" iff this holds for every H of the class.
Parking. White king on file zs rank 1, Black king on file zs rank 6: one square of F_Z on the two ranks where no pawn can stand; never adjacent, never in check. Why it is expected to be neutral: context pawns start on files at distance >= 2 and attack only neighbouring files, so a parked king is never attacked or blocked at the start, and in the frozen model a king move loses at once, so the parked kings never move. This is an expectation, not a proof (a context pawn can reach the buffer file by captures). Neutrality was CHECKED by computation: grp --mode test also solves Psi with a second parking (White king on file zs+1 rank 1, Black king on file zs+fz-1 rank 6) on every context it tests and counts mismatches: parking_mismatch 0 on every line of every run (COMPUTED-1, one code); the K23 referee's ref3 with two parkings gave 0 differences for Z_T (VERIFY.md, claim 1).
T_P (defined here). For a bare group Z (kings and Z-pawns on F_Z, no context) with P value (L,W) (the side to move loses, for both sides to move), a side s to move and a legal move m of s, let d(m) be the exact number of plies in which the opponent wins P after m (a promotion counts as 1 ply; grp2 --depth). T_P(m) = (d(m)+1)/2 = the number of moves the winner makes, the promoting move included. T_P(s) = max over m of T_P(m); this equals half the loss depth of s in the bare group (data/enum_*.txt, columns 2 and 3, are the loss depths 2 T_P(w), 2 T_P(b) in plies). T_P(Z) = max(T_P(w), T_P(b)). T_P = (1,1) is the one-move punishment of Proposition 2.10(a), where the zero is PROVED for every context. T_P(m) >= 2 for some m means that no immediate promotion punishes m. T_P is an exact-P number; the T of Definitions 2.6/2.7 is a bound of the local game (for Z_T: T_P = 5, T = 4), so T_P >= 2 does not by itself give "T >= 2" in that sense; it only excludes the case of 2.10(a).
All 1,236 candidates have T_P(Z) >= 5 (larger loss depth >= 10 plies; maximum 38 plies). In 202 groups one side has T_P = 1. Among the 221 surviving classes (main configurations and d3 runs, screen-level included), 201 have T_P >= 2 on both sides and 20 have T_P = 1 on one side. The four cyl:7x6 survivors have (T_P(w), T_P(b)) = (4,5), (2,8), (6,7), (6,7).

2. CANDIDATES AND THE EXACT ENUMERATION BOUNDARY
scripts/grp.c --mode enum (derived from K23's pk2.c; layers = pawn sets): every group with both kings on any squares of the F_Z files, 1 or 2 white and 0 to 2 black Z-pawns (or 0 to 2 white and 1 or 2 black) on the F_Z files, ranks 2-5, no e.p. right, whose P value is (L,W). 1,236 groups, 446 classes under colour swap with rank flip and the reflection of F_Z (where it maps the board to itself). The referee rebuilt the lists with ref3 (own enumerator): identical in all ten configurations (VERIFY.md, CHECKED-2). (K29's earlier "892" was the wc total of two 446-line files.)
The set contains Z_T's relatives: kings anywhere on F_Z (so the sortie king far from the buffer, next to it, or in the middle), wide F_Z (|F_Z| = 4, the buffer is further from the group), two-file buffers (d3 runs), and groups whose sortie cannot reach the context files before the punisher has won (not a filter: all such groups are in the list). It does not contain: pawns off F_Z, 3 or more Z-pawns of one colour, e.p. layers, ranks 1 and 6.

3. METHOD (what was run)
1. Phase A (scripts/phaseA.sh, grp2 --first 1): every class representative against the first 300 contexts (sorted by number of pawns, then by bit mask; the first 129 are all contexts with at most 2 pawns in total on 8 squares). Stop at the first failing context. One heavy.sh call per configuration (logs/A_*.err).
2. Phase B (scripts/phaseB.py, grp2/grp3): the survivors against the rest of the stated context set, in shards, one heavy.sh call each (logs/B_*.log). For the three-file boards the complete set (4,579 or 14,793 contexts) was too large for the shared slots (about 0.5 CPU-s per group and context beyond the first 300: one shard of 300 contexts of flat:7x6 f3 took 681 CPU-s), so the complete class runs use fewer context files (grp3 --cfiles): the two files at distance 2 on both sides for cyl:8x6 (e,g, both neighbours of the buffer), e,f for flat:7x6 f3, and the single file f for the f4 boards of width 7 and 8 (63 contexts). The other configurations keep the first-300 screen (stated as such).
3. Witness verification (scripts/verify_witness2.sh, scripts/witness2.py): for every failing class the first failing context, both sides to move: Phi by kp_p --pmodel and by ref3, Psi by kpsolve --frozen and ref3 --frozen on the parked-king position. A witness is CONFIRMED iff both P solvers give the same pair, both frozen solvers give the same pair, and Phi != Psi. 278 witnesses (269 in the ten main configurations, 9 in the d3 runs): 278 confirmed, 0 solver disagreements (logs/witness_*_A.txt, logs/witness_cyl7x6_f3.txt). The two c3 witnesses: logs/witness_c3fails.txt.
4. Class-member sample (scripts/witsym.py, scripts/wsym_run.sh): for each main configuration 8-10 random non-representative members of the failing classes, the witness mapped by the symmetry (colour swap with rank flip; reflection of F_Z), solved by the same four codes: 96 members, 96 confirmed (logs/wsym_*.txt).
5. Survivor verification (scripts/chainV.py, scripts/ver2.sh, scripts/cmp2.py): every survivor over EVERY context of its stated set, both sides to move, e.p. "-": Phi by kp_p and ref3, Psi by kpsolve --frozen and ref3 --frozen. Output data/ver_*.cmp (122 lines: 107 main survivors + 15 d3), logs/V_*.log. Every line reads "solver disagreements: Phi 0, Psi 0 ... contexts with Phi != Psi: kp-family 0, ref3 0, either 0".
6. Mechanism (scripts/mech2.py): for each witness, the moves of the deviating side with their P values (kp_p --moves) and in the frozen model.
Solvers: kp_p = K7's private --pmodel build of kpsolve (kings/delegate/out/K7/scripts/draft/kp_p.c); ref3 = the K23 referee's solver written from SPEC.md. kpsolve --frozen and kp_p share one source ("kp family"); ref3 shares nothing with them. grp is derived from K23's pk2.c and is a COMPUTED-1 screening code, not used for a final claim. A bug found on the way: ref3 reads the board as flat7x6, not flat:7x6 (it silently misreads W and H otherwise); chainV.py and verify_witness2.sh pass the right spelling. The old witness.py compared the first two characters of the solver answers (ref3 prints one letter) and reported every witness as a disagreement; witness2.py takes the first token.

 - Kb3 Pa2 Pc2 kb1 pa3 pc3 and Kb1 Pa2 Pb3 ka3 pb2 pc5: no failing context among contexts 0-2681 of the sorted 3,237: all 2,677 contexts with at most 5 pawns in total (1 + 16 + 112 + 448 + 980 + 1,120) and 5 of the 560 six-pawn contexts (COMPUTED-1: one code, grp3; not re-run with a second solver). The six-pawn tier was not run: one 40-context shard used 46 CPU-minutes and 1.8 GB before I killed it. So these two groups are NOT shown to be zeros beside all 3+3 contexts.

5. MECHANISM
mech2.py on the 271 witness lines of the ten main configurations (one line per deviating side; "move class" is that of the first move):
 A, sortie to the buffer (124): the side to move loses in Psi; in P it has a non-losing king step onto a buffer-file square (Z_T's ...Kd2).
 A, stalemate (47): the side to move has no legal move: the bare group's moves are only king steps onto buffer-file squares (checked for all 47 with kp_p --moves), and a context pawn covers all of them; draw instead of loss.
 A, king step inside F_Z only (45): the non-losing first moves stay inside F_Z (the sortie continues later, or the tempo changes the race).
 A, pawn move only (8): the non-losing first moves are Z-pawn or context-pawn moves.
 B, opponent's sortie to the buffer (34): the side to move wins or draws in Psi; every Psi-winning move is refuted in P by a king step of the opponent onto the buffer file.
 B, opponent's king move inside F_Z (13): the same, the refuting reply is a king step inside F_Z.
267 of the 269 first failing contexts of the main configurations have a context pawn on the file at distance exactly 2 (the file next to the buffer); the other two (flat:7x6 f4) have their nearest pawn at distance 3. For the nine d3 witnesses: distance 3 in 8, distance 4 in 1. This extends the K23 observation (every failing context of Z_T had a pawn within a step of the buffer file). It describes the first failing context in sorted order, not all failing contexts, and it is not a necessary condition (the d3 runs show failures two files from the buffer; for example flat:7x6 d3 Ka3 Pb2 kc2 pb3 fails beside Pg2 pg4 pf5).
The timing mechanism of Z_T (the sortie king reaches the buffer and captures a context pawn one tempo before the punisher's win) is the dominant case ("A, sortie to the buffer" and "B, opponent's sortie"). A simple numeric rule does not separate survivors from failures: with e(m) = king moves of the sortie king to a square next to a distance-2 file, plus the capture, the minimum over the sorties of T_P(m) - e(m) (per group, both sides) is 1, -1, 0, 0 on the four cyl:7x6 survivors and between -1 and 6 on the 12 failures (data/S/S_cyl7x6_f3.txt, scripts/sorties2.py, COMPUTED-1). The survivors' sortie kings DO reach the buffer in time; the guess in LOOPY section 8 item 6 ("a sortie king that cannot reach the buffer before the punisher wins") is not what separates them.
CONJECTURE (no hand proof, no mechanism found): Kb3 Pa2 Pc2 kb1 pa3 pc3 and Kb1 Pa2 Pb3 ka3 pb2 pc5 act as 0 beside every context of every size on cyl:7x6 with F_Z = a-c and pawns only on files e,f. Evidence: all 885 contexts of 2+2 (CHECKED-2) and 2,682 of the 3,237 contexts of 3+3 (COMPUTED-1). The two groups that fail at 1+3 show that the 2+2 evidence alone does not carry to larger contexts. No mechanism that forces failure was found for any survivor, and none was proved.

6. CONSEQUENCES FOR LOOPY
- Section 8 item 6 is answered for the class: groups with T_P >= 2 on both sides that act as 0 beside every context of at most 2 pawns a side (on the files at distance >= 2) exist (CHECKED-2: cyl:7x6, cyl:8x6 (contexts on e,g), flat:7x6 (contexts on e,f and on a,g)).
- The CONJECTURE of Proposition 2.10(b) (every group with T >= 2 has a failing context) is NOT refuted: the tested class is bounded, and 2 of the 4 survivors on cyl:7x6 fail beside a larger context. It is false only in the form "every frozen group with T >= 2 fails beside some context of at most 2 pawns a side on the files at distance >= 2".

7. EXACT COMMANDS (under kings/delegate/out/K29/; heavy ones through kings/delegate/heavy.sh)
